domain: tropical cyclone best track (Japan Meteorological Agency, RSMC Tokyo-Typhoon Center, western North Pacific)
prediction_question: Formulation considered: from a tropical cyclone's JMA best-track state and history through the 6-hourly analysis time t (position, central pressure, maximum sustained wind, storm grade, past-24h track), predict whether the cyclone undergoes rapid intensification (RI) in the following 24 hours (Vmax increase >= 30 kt). NOT taken forward: the same prediction question already ships in ML-ready, split, scored form elsewhere (TCRISI: satellite-image + best-track RI benchmark with official train/validation/test splits and a benchmark repository; TCBench: IBTrACS-based TC track/intensity benchmark with year-based splits), so a best-track-only RI task is a mirror of an existing usable task, not a contribution.
prediction_time: For the rejected formulation only: the 6-hourly best-track analysis instant t (all track parameters through t knowable); the label is the change in the same storm's final-analysis Vmax over the following 24 h, so rows at t+24h.. are label source. Best track is a post-season final analysis, which is the documented grain of the source, not a leakage defect.
target_definition: Binary RI: Vmax(t+24h) - Vmax(t) >= 30 kt. Unit/reference-frame caveat recorded before the rejection was reached: the 30 kt/24 h RI standard is defined on 1-minute sustained winds (Kaplan & DeMaria convention), while JMA best-track winds are 10-minute sustained, so a JMA-units task would need an explicit threshold decision and a known-event fixture; this question is moot because the task is a mirror.

rejection_reason: Mirror of an existing usable task. The prediction question this source most naturally supports - rapid intensification in the next 24 h from track parameters - already ships as scored, split, ML-ready benchmarks: (1) TCRISI (National Taiwan University, Hsuan-Tien Lin's group, csie.ntu.edu.tw/~htlin/program/TCRISI) - 'serves as the dataset for benchmarking the performance of TC rapid intensification prediction models', derived from the TCIR satellite-image + best-track dataset, with published training/validation/test splits and an official benchmark repository for loading tfrecords, plus benchmark results (Bai, Chen & Lin, attention-based deep models); (2) TCBench (arXiv 2601.23268, 2026) - an IBTrACS-derived benchmark for TC track and intensity with year-based storm splits and named baselines; (3) a research literature with public SHIPS predictor data (rammb2.cira.colostate.edu) and chronological train/test splits (e.g. Springer Nat Hazards 2023: train 1982-2015 vs test 2016-2020, RI = DELV >= 30 kt/24 h). Data mirrors of the raw source also exist (IBTrACS republishes RSMC Tokyo best track; Digital Typhoon archive; the jmastats R package reads best-track files directly). Per the standing rule, an existing packaged task with splits and scored models makes this a rejection regardless of how clean the JMA channel is: access (one anonymous 0.75 MB GET) and licence (Public Data License v1.0) were the best measured in this tick's region, which is exactly why the task-level check had to be applied before any construction was spent.
next_action: None - terminal. Recorded so a future tick does not re-open JMA blind: the other JMA families are also family-level duplications of candidates already on the bench - JMA earthquake felt-intensity duplicates the bmkg-earthquake-felt family (parked on label availability, not on source access), and MLIT river-level exceedance duplicates the malaysia-river-danger-exceedance family. Reopening either needs an explicit operator decision naming the family, per the air4thai precedent. If a genuinely different JMA-anchored task is ever sought, it must first pass the same search for an existing packaged task that this record's RI formulation failed.

novelty_check.theirs: A packaged, split, scored RI prediction task (TCRISI; TCBench for track/intensity forecasting), the raw best-track data from multiple channels including the publisher itself, and a mature literature with public predictors.
novelty_check.ours: Nothing: a best-track-only RI task would be a thinner re-cut of benchmarks that already exist with splits and scored results. The channel quality (open licence, one-file bulk) is access, not contribution.
novelty_check.rule: A dataset that already exists in ML-ready form is not published. Mirroring is a failure mode, not a contribution.
